newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-LEADING MEN AT AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-LEADING MEN AT AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Portraits of the leading male challengers at the Australian Open, starting on Monday.

Despite his triumph at the U.S. Open, 1996 proved a mediocre year for the world number one. For the first time since 1992, the 25-year-old American failed to win at least two of the four grand slam tournaments on offer. Only one of his eight grand slams to date has been achieved on the Rebound Ace hardcourt in Melbourne, in 1994. On his last visit to Australia, he was ambushed by local hero Mark Philippoussis in the third round. Sampras ended the year by beating Boris Becker in an epic final at the ATP Tour World Championship to capture his third win in the prestigious tournament.
Seeded: 1. Age: 25. Weight: 77kg. Height: 1.85m. Ranking: 1. Tournament wins: 44. First round opponent: (Dinu Pescariu, qualifier).

A tireless worker who compensates for his lack of height and power with astonishing speed around the court, Chang experienced a mixed year in 1996. Beaten in the first round at Wimbledon and two rounds later at the French Open, the scene in 1989 of his only grand slam win, the American compensated by reaching the final at the Australian Open and U.S. Open, only to be beaten by Boris Becker and Pete Sampras respectively. His consistent tour performances lifted the game's most prominent Christian to second in the rankings, the highest of his career.
Seeded: 2. Age: 24. Weight: 68kg. Height: 1.75m. Ranking: 2. Tournament wins: 26. First round opponent: (Kris Goossens qualifier).

After a disappointing season during which he failed to reach any grand slam finals, the temperamental Croat is becomining acutely aware of his inability to win the big ones. As usual, his serve proved the most lethal on tour, yielding him 1,477 aces and helping him to five tournaments wins on the ATP Tour and five other finals, a career record for a single season. Ivanisevic has never progressed beyond the quarter-final stage in Melbourne but will enjoy his usual heavy support from the city's vociferous Croatian community. If he can control or channel his excitement, Ivanisevic could finally break through in Melbourne.
Seeded 3. Age: 25. Weight: 82kg. Height: 1.94. Ranking: 3. Tournament wins: 17. First round opponent: Ben Ellwood (Australia, wildcard)

The elder statesman of men's tennis following the retirement of Sweden's Stefan Edberg, Becker started 1996 with victory in the Australian Open to end a five-year spell without a grand slam win. His fortunes dipped when a serious wrist tendon injury forced him out for long periods. The German Davis Cup player, who has won twice in Melbourne, returned to beat Sampras in Stuttgart and the round-robin stage at the ATP World Championship in November only to lose a five-set final to the world number one. A self-confessed slow starter in major events, he faces a tough first round match against Spain's Carlos Moya.
Seeded: 6. Age: 29. Weight: 85kg. Height: 1.90m. Ranking: 6. Tournament wins: 49. First round opponent: Carlos Moya (Spain)

An outsider who sent his success-starved compatriots into a nationalistic fervour when he reached the Wimbledon quarter-finals last year before succumbing to American Todd Martin. Henman leapt 70 places in the rankings in 1996 to finish the year at 29 before surging to the final in Qatar and then winning the Sydney International on Saturday, a feat that eluded his revered countryman Fred Perry, the last Englishman to win Wimbledon in 1936. Henman was to have faced hard-hitting Mark Philippoussis in the first round, but must have been relieved to hear on Sunday that Philippoussis was withdrawing because of tendinitis. He will instead play a "lucky loser" from the qualifying tournament.
Not seeded. Age: 22. Weight: 70kg. Height: 1.85m. Ranking: 24. Tournament wins: 1. First round opponent: Andre Pavel (Romania).
